title: Derived completeness of limits of elementwise nilpotent torsion complexes
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal, and let $(L_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system in $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose that for every $f\in I$ and every $n$ there exists an integer $e\geq1$ such that the endomorphism $f^e:L_n\to L_n$ is zero in $D(A)$. Then $R\varprojlim_nL_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] is derived complete with respect to $I$ [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]: for every $f\in I$ the derived limit of the constant system on this object with transitions multiplication by $f$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 091W, lemma-naive-derived-completion, specialization with the tensor factor K=A[0]

proof.text: Fix a level n and f in I. To verify derived completeness [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex], take any product structure on the constant tower with value L_n and any derived-limit Roos triangle [def-weil-derived-limit]. Choose e with f^e id(L_n)=0. Let s be the weighted product shift [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Induction and product extensionality [def-weil-category-product] give s^r followed by projection j equal to f^r times projection j+r. At r=e, each component vanishes: it is projection j+e followed by f^e id(L_n). Therefore s^e=0. The ring of endomorphisms and Mathlib IsNilpotent.isUnit_one_sub give invertibility of 1-s, equivalently CategoryTheory.isUnit_iff_isIso.

Mathlib Pretriangulated.Triangle.isZero₁_of_isIso₂ applied to the distinguished Roos triangle shows its first object is zero. This is the standard consequence of triangle exactness [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] and rotation [def-weil-triangulated-category] already proved in Mathlib. Thus every L_n is derived I-complete [def-weil-point-derived-complete-module-complex]. No existence theorem is necessary: the definition quantifies over product structures and derived limits already given.

Apply the product clause of [lem-weil-pbc-module-derived-complete-products-triangles] to the complete objects L_n and the product structure supplied in the hypotheses. This proves completeness of Q=product L_n. Unpack the given derived-limit hypothesis [def-weil-derived-limit] to obtain its distinguished triangle H to Q to Q to H[1]. Apply the second-and-third-vertices case of the triangle clause of the same closure lemma to obtain derived completeness of H. Each chosen exponent depends only on its own f and n; no common exponent is used.
